guide.summary: The Minster, city walls and museums of York, with breakfast cafés, a bakery, dinners and cocktail bars checked against their own websites.
guide.tip: York Art Gallery opens Wednesday to Sunday only, with entry in 30-minute slots, Skosh is closed Sunday to Tuesday and Roots York on Mondays and Tuesdays, so plan early-week dinners elsewhere.

toolkit.label: Closing days
toolkit.copy: York Art Gallery opens Wednesday to Sunday, Skosh is closed Sunday to Tuesday and Roots York is closed Monday and Tuesday. York Cold War Bunker opens Friday to Sunday and bank holidays only.

toolkit.label: Tickets
toolkit.copy: A York Minster sightseeing ticket is valid for a whole calendar year and includes four children aged 17 and under, and York Castle Museum tickets give entry for 12 months. Clifford's Tower's online discount is available until midnight the day before your visit.

toolkit.label: Booking and walk-ins
toolkit.copy: The National Railway Museum is free but recommends booking in busy periods, and York Castle Museum advises pre-booking on Saturdays and in school holidays. The Star Inn the City takes no reservations for drinks only, while Skosh offers walk-in seating in its bar area.

toolkit.label: Rules
toolkit.copy: Station Hall at the National Railway Museum is card only, and York Cold War Bunker is visited by pre-booked guided tour only. Skosh asks for card details to secure a table and charges £20 per person for cancellations with less than 24 hours' notice.

guide.dek: Book the Minster and the Castle Museum first, then plan dinners around restaurants that close early in the week.
intro: York Minster on Deangate is the anchor of most visits. Its own site gives first admission at 9:30am and last admission at 4pm, and says it is open every day of the year but may close occasionally for services, so you should check its calendar. A sightseeing ticket is valid for a whole calendar year and includes four children aged 17 and under. From 28 November the Minster lists a Christmas Tree Festival running to 5 January 2027. The City of York Council says you can walk the city walls on foot, for free, throughout the year.

The National Railway Museum on Leeman Road is free and opens daily from 10am to 5pm except 24 to 26 December. It recommends booking in busy periods, and building work continues as part of its Masterplan; Station Hall is card only. York Castle Museum at the Eye of York sells tickets valid for 12 months and advises pre-booking on Saturdays and in school holidays. York Art Gallery on Exhibition Square opens Wednesday to Sunday in 30-minute entry slots and is showing Turner, Wedgwood & Beyond: Inspired by Flaxman. The Yorkshire Museum sits in the free Museum Gardens.

Smaller sites reward a slower day. Fairfax House on Castlegate is closed from 2 to 13 November 2026 to install its Christmas exhibition, A Christmas Tail, which opens on 14 November. York's Chocolate Story on King's Square lists Christmas tours and masterclasses from 28 November to 23 December 2026. Clifford's Tower on Tower Street opens daily from 10am to 4pm, with last entry at 3:30pm. Out of the centre, York Cold War Bunker on Monument Close opens Friday to Sunday and bank holidays, by pre-booked guided tour only.

For breakfast, Partisan on Micklegate serves an all-day breakfast and brunch menu from 9am to 3pm daily, and The Star Inn the City in the Lendal Engine House opens at 9.30am on Fridays to Sundays. For dinner, Skosh on Micklegate takes bookings Wednesday to Saturday, Roots York on Marygate offers set menus from £110, and The Bow Room at Grays Court serves its tasting menu Wednesday to Saturday at 7pm. Evil Eye and The Botanist share Stonegate for drinks, and The Botanist runs a weekday happy hour from 4pm to 7pm.
summaryCards: Pair York Minster with a walk on the free city walls and an afternoon at the free National Railway Museum.
Start with breakfast at Partisan or Spring Espresso, then walk through the Museum Gardens to the Yorkshire Museum.
Check closing days, since York Art Gallery opens Wednesday to Sunday Skosh closes Sunday to Tuesday and Roots York closes Mondays and Tuesdays.

limitations: Website review, not a visit or telephone confirmation. Advertised opening, booking and exhibition details do not guarantee availability. Several sites could not be read: Jorvik Viking Centre and Barley Hall returned 403, Treasurer's House showed a bot check, Bettys and Merchant Adventurers' Hall returned empty pages, and several smaller cafés and bars failed on DNS, certificate or connection errors; none of these failures is evidence of closure. Weekly hours were not published on the pages read for Middlethorpe Hall, The Grand, York and Ate O'Clock, and the City Walls opening-times page returned 404. Spring Espresso, Bluebird Bakery and Partisan showed current hours and menus but no dated 2026 content. The National Railway Museum is mid-redevelopment, so gallery access may change.
